title: `AppendCheckpointTrailer` can emit a trailer the final-block parser (and git) reject

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers moving the trailer logic into the trailers package and deduplicating it, but never mentions how indented trailer-shaped lines are treated. The looser TrimSpace-based grammar in the writer was carried along by refactors, not chosen as a decision.

- Move trailer manipulation (AppendCheckpointTrailer, IsTrailerLine) to

  it's Gemini-specific transcript logic
- Extract transcript utilities (extractTranscriptMetadata,
  estimateSessionDuration) to attach_transcript.go
- Replace hardcoded agentSessionBaseDirs map with SessionBaseDirProvider
  optional interface on Agent, implemented by Claude Code, Gemini CLI,
  Cursor, and Factory AI Droid
- Fix storeTranscript parameter ordering: ctx first per Go convention
- Distinguish "detection failed" from "no changes found" in attach output
- Switch estimateSessionDuration from bytes.Split to bufio.Scanner
- Simplify resolveAndValidateTranscript by removing redundant agentName
  parameter

Simplify: fix Scanner bug, remove dual-context, deduplicate trailer logic

- Revert estimateSessionDuration from bufio.Scanner back to bytes.Split:
  Scanner has a 64KB default line limit that silently truncates large
  JSONL lines (tool results can easily exceed this). Since data is
  already in memory, bytes.Split has no memory overhead and no limit.
- Remove dual-context (ctx, logCtx) from collectFileChanges, matching
  the fix already applied to storeTranscript. No other function in the
  codebase takes two context parameters.
- Replace addCheckpointTrailer in manual_commit_hooks.go with a
  one-line delegation to trailers.AppendCheckpointTrailer, eliminating
  55 lines of duplicated trailer-appending logic.

worker.report:
`AppendCheckpointTrailer` now starts a new paragraph when the message ends in an indented pseudo-trailer. It no longer glues the new trailer onto that paragraph. `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/trailers/ -run 'TestAppendCheckpointTrailer'` passes. That pattern also runs the existing `TestAppendCheckpointTrailer` cases, so the old behaviours still pass. I did not run the rest of the suite.

The new test failed on the old code for the space-indented case, the tab-indented case and the continuation-line case.

I did not extract a shared `isTrailerBlock` out of `finalTrailerBlock`, as the issue proposes. In this tree `finalTrailerBlock` still trims whitespace and has no continuation handling, so it isn't the stricter reader the issue describes. I added `isTrailerBlock` for the writer only and left the reader alone, to keep the change small. The two now disagree in the other direction: the reader still accepts an indented checkpoint line that the writer now treats as plain body text.

`appendTrailerLine` now collects the final paragraph as raw lines, still skipping comment lines. It joins the new trailer onto that paragraph only if a blank line separates it from the content above and `isTrailerBlock` holds. `isTrailerBlock` needs at least one real trailer line, and every other line must be an indented continuation of a trailer before it.

The continuation case from the issue (`Signed-off-by: ...` followed by ` continuation text`) now stays one block, with no blank line inserted.

Test name: `TestAppendCheckpointTrailer_IndentedPseudoTrailer`
Files changed: `cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/trailers/append_indented_test.go` (new)
